data.title: Middle East Eye: Iran-backed Iraqi group refuses to withdraw from stronghold
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Iran-backed Iraqi group refuses to withdraw from stronghold
Kataeb Hezbollah, Iraq's Iran-backed paramilitary group, said it will not leave its stronghold despite the US-backed prime minister calling on the armed faction to withdraw and allow the army to enter.
On Monday, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi gave Kataeb Hezbollah an unspecified deadline to withdraw from Jurf al-Sakher, south of Baghdad, after the government earlier said an investigative committee had confirmed oil smuggling in the area - a claim the armed group denied.
"I can state decisively and with absolute certainty that the dream they dream of the Kataeb withdrawing from Jurf al-Sakher will not come true, not even over our dead bodies," Abu Taleb al-Saidi, a Kataeb Hezbollah commander, told AFP during a press visit to the area.
A security source told AFP that the deadline for Kataeb Hezbollah to withdraw from the area south of Baghdad was on Friday.
Saidi stressed that his group did not want a confrontation with Iraqi armed forces.

At 9pm every night during the first weeks of Israel's genocide in Gaza, around 30 people and their children in the home where I was displaced would gather in an empty space in front of the house.
Many of them wrapped themselves in woollen blankets, some sitting on the ground, others standing, looking for their daily "dose of hope" on a television screen.
With no electricity, we used the little power the available solar panels could collect from the sun all day to turn on the TV and watch the news for around 30 minutes.
Once the familiar news theme played, those gathering around the screen started calling on others inside the house to hurry and join them.
Among them, I stood, very well aware that those sparkling eyes would not find what they were looking for.
They would find no international action taken against the war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide we were witnessing, no appropriate international condemnation, and not even a statement by a world leader clearly naming the perpetrators.
Sitting on a concrete bench with an old displaced man from the shelter next to ours who came to watch the news with us, I whispered: "Do you still hope to see meaningful international action taken this time?"
He told me he was not watching the news in anticipation of any action by world governments, but found solace in seeing updates about the protests sweeping the streets of countries around the world.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iraq resumes shipping oil for export to Turkey via pipeline
data.author: MEE staff
data.summary:
Iraq resumes shipping oil for export to Turkey via pipeline
Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Tue, 11/17/2026 - 20:00
Iraqi oil minister says Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline could reach capacity of 500,000 bpd with repairs and upgrades
An Iraqi government forces member walks next to a pipeline at the Bai Hassan Oil Field, west of the northern Iraqi city of Kirkuk, on 19 October 2017 (Ahmad al-Rubaye/AFP)
Off
Iraq has resumed the pumping of crude oil for export through the Kirkuk-Ceyhan Pipeline to Turkey, as it looks to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.
Iraq plans to pump up to 120,000 barrels per day (bpd) of oil through the 960km-long pipeline that runs from the Iraqi city to Turkey’s Mediterranean port, Iraqi Oil Minister Bassem Khudair said in a statement reported by the state-owned Iraqi News Agency on Tuesday.
He said the flow could reach 500,000 bpd after “successful completion of maintenance, rehabilitation, technical and operational tests” on the pipeline, which has been shuttered for more than a decade.
Iraq is one of the countries hardest hit by the US and Iran’s competing blockades in the Strait of Hormuz. Nearly all of Iraq’s oil exports exited the waterway before the US-Israeli war on Iran, and revenue from sales contributed to 90 percent of Iraq’s budget.
Restarting oil flows from Kirkuk to Ceyhan is the first step in Iraq’s efforts to reduce its dependence on Hormuz. Baghdad wants to connect Basra, its energy hub in southern Iraq, to the Mediterranean via the Syrian port of Baniyas and Turkey’s port of Ceyhan.
Middle East Eye was the first to report US efforts to revive a pipeline connection between Kirkuk and Baniyas. US ambassador to Iraq Tom Barrack hailed the reopening of the Kirkuk-Ceyhan line on Tuesday in a post on social media.
“Go Iraq, Go,” Barrack wrote.

Off
A 42-year-old Palestinian-American writer has emerged as the first challenger to Pennsylvania Democratic Senator and staunch pro-Israel ally John Fetterman in his 2028 Senate race.
It's not too uncommon for US candidates to declare their bid this early. Election campaigns in this country run for at least 18 months before every election, giving voters little reprieve from the ads and media placements.
Speaking to Middle East Eye on Monday, Ahmed Moor said he is centring three foreign policy priorities. "End the war in Iran. End the war in Ukraine. End the war on the Palestinians."
The slogan echoes the successful platforms of those who undoubtedly paved the way for him: Democratic Socialist New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, and Democratic Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed.
Though in his conversation with MEE, he did not seem to want the comparison to be made.
Moor is also an immigrant, an Arab, a Muslim, a millennial, a progressive, a passionate proponent of Palestinian rights, and a father of three girls. Sayed has two children, and played up his "girl dad" persona.
Was Moor inspired?
"I'm a man of the left," he responded, sticking strictly to his campaign message. "We're going to have the left-right contest in America all the time. What this campaign is about is the shape of the sandbox. The idea that the Constitution and Bill of Rights is under assault is not a left-right issue. That's an American issue."

Israeli parliament elects Eisenkot ally as speaker in blow for Netanyahu
Israeli lawmakers on Tuesday elected Matan Kahana, a parliament speaker from the camp opposed to caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Sixty-six of 120 lawmakers voted in favour of Kahana, an ally of former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, who has until next month to form a government to replace Netanyahu.
Netanyahu's Likud party had put forward Ofir Katz as its own candidate, who received 52 votes.
The parliament speaker is an important office given that it sets the timetable for parliamentary business and can therefore speed up or delay debates or votes on proposed legislation.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Rubio says 'no imminent threat' to US from Iran
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Rubio says 'no imminent threat' to US from Iran
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio cast doubt about reports of an "imminent threat" from Iran on Washington.
Speaking to reporters in the Philippines, Rubio said that US authorities routinely check for potential threats against the country, but added that most intelligence leads are not considered credible.
When asked if he was concerned about a possible attack on Washington, he said: "I am not. But again, we're concerned every day about anything that threatens our country ... I don't think there's any imminent threat."
"The United States is always on the lookout for anyone who tries to do harm to our country and to our people. And we have threat streams every day, and the majority of them are not credible. We have to follow up on them," Rubio added.
Rubio also questioned the credibility of sources cited in a CNN report about an alleged Iranian plot targeting the US capital, saying: "Some of your intelligence sources are liars; others are liars and criminals."
"I won't even comment on it because I don't know who's leaking this stuff to you guys. But they're either showboats and liars, or probably criminals if they're saying anything that's even half true."

data.title: Middle East Eye: Watch: Israeli settles kill Palestinian grandmother in occupied West Bank
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Watch: Israeli settles kill Palestinian grandmother in occupied West Bank
Israeli settlers shot dead an elderly Palestinian woman and wounded eight of her family members during an attack outside her home in the village of Ein al-Duyuk al-Tahta, west of Jericho in the occupied West Bank.
According to eyewitnesses, armed settlers shot 73-year-old Fidda Fheidat in the head, killing her on the spot.
The settlers, who had recently seized eight Palestinian homes in an area adjacent to the village, went on to fire at other members of the family, wounding eight of them.
According to Jihad Mahalis, a member of the village’s local committee, the settlers have launched attacks on the village homes every single night since seizing the properties, which are located some 500 metres away from the rest of the village’s homes.

Bahrain's civil defence evacuates multi-storey building due to fire
Bahrain’s Ministry of Interior said that civil defence teams evacuated a multi-storey building in the Gulf country's north west due to a fire.
"Civil Defence evacuated a multi-story building in Souq Waqif as a precaution, and extinguished a fire in the building. No injuries were reported," the ministry said in a statement.
"The National Ambulance took the necessary measures at the site, and investigations are underway to determine the cause of the fire," it added.
